Commentary.Commentary: We are back with New Zealand's reply to a total of 205 from the West Indies. Tom Latham and Devon Conway have walked out for New Zealand, whereas Kemar Roach will be bowling the first over of this contest.
... SECOND INNINGS ...

The Black Caps' bowling was a masterclass, expertly reeling in the Windies after letting them off to a solid start but bouncing back. Blair Tickner stormed back in the post-lunch session with a devastating spell, claiming 4 wickets in total, while Michael Rae took 3, and Glenn Phillips and Jacob Duffy added one each. However, Tickner's injury woes resurfaced, dislocating his right shoulder, leaving doubts over his participation in the contest and potentially leaving the Kiwis a bowler short.

The West Indies' chances fizzle out in a heap. A solid 153 for 3 had them cruising, but a calamitous collapse sees them crumble for 205. Shai Hope's departure was the turning point, triggering a horrific slide where the last 7 wickets tumble for next to nothing. The top and middle order, John Campbell, Brandon King, Shai Hope, and Roston Chase, all got starts, but converting them into big scores proved elusive, and it was a case of 'so near, yet so far' for the Windies.

The West Indies' bright start is snatched away as they implode to 205 all out! Blair Tickner's sizzling bowling, paired with Michael Rae's pinpoint accuracy, has absolutely bulldozed through the Windies' batting line-up, leaving them in tatters against the scorching New Zealand attack.

… DAY 1, SECOND SESSION …

New Zealand need to attack the stumps and bowl fuller to the opposition batter. They are often dishing the fuller deliveries away from the stump, which is giving the Chevrons' batters to drive without any fear, as the ball is not swinging much. The two wickets they got were from the deliveries that attacked the stumps. On the other hand, Shai Hope and John Campbell will look to extend their partnership till the end of the Tea Break. John Campbell is on 44 and he is just six runs away from his fourth half-century. But for now, grab some coffee or snacks till the end of the Lunch break and come back around 12.40 am GMT to witness the action in the second session.

The day started with a strong partnership of John Campbell and Brandon King, who had a knot of 66 runs partnership. They were pretty confident till the end of the drinks break, but after that, the LBW of Blair Tickner boosted the Kiwis. After the dismissal of King, Kavem Hodge stepped on the crease and got dismissed by Tickner in the same fashion he had eliminated King. However, after that, the previous test's centurion, Shai Hope, stepped on the crease and eased the situation. Campbell is looking sturdy since he entered the green turf. There were quite a few moments where he got an inside edg,e but the ball bounces away from the wickets, but other than that, he is doing really well to keep the Chevrons up front.

SESSION SUMMARY - 27 overs, 92 runs and 2 wickets. Well, if we look back to the first session of this day, we can say that the Chevrons are having a bit upper hand. They have really scored 100 runs and if they continue this till the end of the day, we can see them ending the day with more than 240-250 and then they can continue fresh tomorrow. But again, this is cricket and we all have seen things happening in this game.

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the pre-match formalities.The umpires are out to the middle and New Zealand players take their respective field positions. John Campbell and Brandon King will be the openers for West Indies. Jacob Duffy has the red cherry in his hands. Off we go...

We are moments away from the start of the game, but before that, the players from both sides make their way out to the middle and line up for the respective national anthems. It will be West Indies' first followed by that of New Zealand's.

PITCH REPORT - Mark Richardson described the pitch as having a nice, even covering of grass, although it wasn't as green as expected for a Day 1 surface at this venue. He noted that the pitch seemed to be drying out faster than others, making it uncertain whether it would favor batting or offer some movement. Richardson praised the surface, stating it would likely offer some life throughout the game, making it an exciting Test match pitch. He added that losing the toss wouldn't be the end of the world, but acknowledged that New Zealand would be happy to bowl first on this surface, provided they bowl well.

Skipper of West Indies, Roston Chase, says that mentions that they would have preferred bowling first, given the wicket's green appearance. He emphasizes the need to bat well, considering the conditions. He praises their batting department for their endurance, bowling over 160 overs, and their bowling performance, restricting New Zealand to under 250. The team has made three changes as Anderson Phillip replaces Johann Layne, Kavem Hodge is included, and Tagenarine Chanderpaul is out due to an injury.

Tom Latham, skipper of New Zealand, says that they are going to bowl first. Adds that winning the toss and bowling first is a tradition on this track. Continues that they have to see how the pitch behaves on the deliveries and then shape their batting according to that. Also states that in Basin, the wicket gets better as the game rolls on. Also says that they are all pumped up. It ends up saying that they have four changes, with Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips set to be in the starting XI. Additionally, they have two debutants, as Mitchell Hay and Michael Rae are also in the playing XI.
New Zealand (Playing XI) - Tom Latham (C), Devon Conway, Kane Williamson, Rachin Ravindra, Daryl Mitchell, Mitchell Hay (WK), Glenn Phillips, Zakary Foulkes, Blair Tickner, Jacob Duffy, Michael Rae.
West Indies (Playing XI) - John Campbell, Brandon King, Kavem Hodge, Shai Hope, Roston Chase (C), Justin Greaves, Tevin Imlach (WK), Kemar Roach, Jayden Seales, Anderson Phillip, Ojay Shields.
TOSS - Tom Latham has won the coin flip and elected to BOWL first.

The West Indies, meanwhile, will be riding a wave of confidence and buzz not felt in years. That 'Herculean effort' in Christchurch proved their resilience and ability to bat for long periods. The challenge now for Roston Chase's side is to produce a more consistent performance, particularly in their first innings, where they were dismissed for a mere 167 in the first Test. They can't rely on miracles in every game. If they can replicate the patience and fight shown by Justin Greaves, Kemar Roach, and Shai Hope earlier in the match, they might pose a serious threat to a win in Wellington.

For the Black Caps, the focus shifts to Wellington's Basin Reserve with a need to close out matches when in dominant positions. They had West Indies at 72-4 in the fourth innings, chasing an impossible 531, but failed to secure the final six wickets. Captain Tom Latham will be looking for his bowlers to be more clinical and perhaps benefit from a less depleted attack, after injuries to key seamers Matt Henry and Nathan Smith impacted their ability to finish the job. The hosts will be buzzing to right that wrong and leverage home advantage to go one-nil up in the series. It will be interesting to see on who replaces Smith and Henry if they have not yet recovered.

Hello and welcome, cricket fans from around the globe, to the much-anticipated build-up for the second Test match between New Zealand and West Indies! The series has already set the tone with one of the most remarkable Test matches in recent history at Hagley Oval in Christchurch. The first Test ended in a thrilling draw after the West Indies, following on the brink of defeat, produced a legendary fourth-innings performance. Justin Greaves' unbeaten double century (202) and Kemar Roach's monumental resistance saw them achieve the highest fourth-innings total in a five-day Test and secure a famous draw, etching their names in the annals of cricket history.
